en: The Triplet on the Visible (Sanidassanattika) and the Dyad on the Possessing an Object (Sārammaṇaduka)
Dependent on a phenomenon that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and with an object, there arises a phenomenon that is neither non-demonstrable nor non-reactive and without an object,

by way of root condition. Dependent on a phenomenon that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and with an object, there arises a phenomenon that is neither non-demonstrable nor reactive and without an object,
by way of root condition …pe… dependent on a phenomenon that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and with an object … [and so forth].
Dependent on states that are non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and without an object, there arise states that are non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and without an object by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. There are six [conditions] for the root; six for the predominance ... pe ... three for mutuality ...

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and without an object, there arises a state that is neither demonstrable nor reactive and without an object, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition there are three.
